summary: Phase 1 fails acceptance at f0a6fdaa5988 on one blocker, F1. The D8 rule, the Results table, and the route result match judge-r1.json and arm-key.json. Task 4, the spend rule, the foreign-hunk rule, and the wash-basin mechanical check also hold. F1: the promoted Hy4 wash-basin is 0.494 m deep against a 0.40 m brief, which is 23.5 percent over. The judge brief sets the wrong-scale line at 20 percent, the judge saw no sizes, and no gate checks size. The pass of this card decides the route result, so the owner must rule or the judge must rerate.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] phase-acceptance: The promoted wash-basin (source wash-basin-a, Hy4 arm) measures 0.419 x 0.199 x 0.494 m (out/wash-basin/stats.json, rebuilt by my rerun). The brief size is 0.42 x 0.17 x 0.40 m (measure/tracks/asset_hy4_maker_trial_20261116/briefs/wash-basin.md:10). The depth is 23.5 percent over. The other three horizontal extents are 0.21 m from the centre (stats.json: min x -0.21, max x 0.21, min z -0.21). Only the dipper reaches z 0.284 m (handle cone: assets/wash-basin.ts:229, from z 0.115 to z 0.27). Rule broken: measure/runs/asset_hy4_maker_trial_20261116/judge-brief.md:66 caps a card at 7.0 for a wrong scale, which is a size more than 20 percent away from the brief. judge-brief.md:81 lists a wrong scale as critical error 4, and a critical error fails a card whatever its rating. Spec D6 (spec.md:138) passes a card only with no critical model error. The judge gave this card 8.0 with pass true and critical empty (judge-r1.json, card wash-basin-a). Rationale: the judge could not measure, because the cards show no sizes. mech-check.mjs:53 holds the only size test, the bottom y, so no gate compares size to the brief. The plan lists the height overrun (17 percent) and the rack width overrun (11 percent) as known misses (plan.md:103), but not this depth. This card decides the route result. If wrong scale is a critical error, wash-basin-a fails and the current arm wins wash-basin. Then Hy4 wins 1 of 3, and the route result at plan.md:169 changes. If only the 7.0 cap applies, the new rating is 7.0 or less: a tie at 7.0, and a fail below 7.0. A tie changes plan.md:163 and plan.md:169, keeps the route rule, and keeps the promotion (arm a wins the D9 tie-break). Owner of the fix: the user decides the ruling (ESCALATE). The Measure orchestrator (build session) records the ruling in plan.md and reruns the judge with measured sizes. measure-jr-green (Green) re-promotes assets/wash-basin.ts from wash-basin-b (commit 6a03ea7e) only if wash-basin-a fails. Rerun this acceptance at the new HEAD.
